why: The routes that decide who somebody is are the ones an attacker reaches first and the ones a product change reaches last. Each rule here is checked against the route table, the migration history and the analytics vocabulary rather than against a list, so a route added tomorrow is measured the day it lands.

rateLimit.why: an unthrottled credential endpoint is a free guessing machine

audit.why: a sign-in nobody recorded cannot be disputed, revoked or explained afterwards

defects.why: linking mints the pairing code the approval consumes, so a trail that starts at approval cannot say which device asked
defects.fix: add an entry for device/link/route.ts to UNAUDITED_MUTATING_ROUTES in apps/web/lib/services/audit-coverage/registry.ts with reason no_governed_state, or record the code it mints

session.why: an identity resolved a second way is a second set of rules nobody keeps in step

cookies.why: a session cookie without all three is readable by script, sent in the clear or attached to somebody else's form post

defects.why: a bearer token in a plain text column is a bearer token in every backup and every replica of that backup
defects.fix: drop the column; every statement in apps/web/app/api/device and apps/web/app/api/auth/device writes NULL to it, so nothing reads a value from it

defects.why: the refresh half of the same pair, and the one that does not expire in minutes
defects.fix: drop the column in the same migration as access_token

analytics.why: an analytics property is copied to a third party by definition, so a credential-shaped key is an exfiltration route with a dashboard on the end
